decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'if I try to save a link I've already got, it warns me and takes me to the one I already saved instead of making a duplicate' / 'duplicate detection'. R1 client: 'I really like that if I try to save a link I've already got, it warns me and takes me to the one I already saved instead of making a duplicate — that's exactly what I'd want.'
decisions.note: Prototype/spec-gate. Duplicate-save convergence to editing conforms to REF-BM-06; recorded conforming decision, client approves.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'saving/editing/deleting bookmarks, tags, ... search, filtering, sorting, ... persistent storage.' R1 client: 'Saving links, editing and deleting them, tags, searching, filtering by tag, sorting, and having everything stick around between visits all sound right.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Core CRUD, tags, tag-filter, basic search, sort and persistence conform to the reference; recorded conforming decision approved by the client.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented 'favorites'. R1 client: 'you've got "favorites," but the thing I actually had in mind is being able to flag a link as "read this later," and then have a way to look at just those unread ones, and check them off as read once I've gotten to them. That "to-read" idea matters more to me than a favorites star.' R2 maker: 'Read-later states replacing favorites.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presentation offered favorites instead of the reference read-later/unread model; client rejects it and supplies the reference-conforming read-later + unread view + mark-read behaviour (REF-BM-17/18/19).

decisions.evidence: R1 maker spec required hand-typing; client: 'when I save a link, I don't want to have to type in the title myself. I'd expect the app to go look at the page and fill in the title for me automatically — and ideally a short description and the little site icon too. I'd still want to be able to tweak that text ... both when I'm saving and later.' R2 maker: 'Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval, with editable text.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presentation contradicted REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description/favicon) by requiring manual title entry; client supplies the reference behaviour plus editability (REF-BM-03) in place of the mismatch.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'link previews are out of scope.' The auto-fetch scope (R2: title, description, site-icon) never includes a preview image. R1 client: 'On the things you've put out of scope ... I understand leaving out sharing, folders, browser add-ons, and page previews for now.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. REF-BM-02 also mandates capturing a preview image; the maker excluded 'page/link previews' and the client explicitly identifies and accepts that departure without requesting alignment — accepted divergence (distinct sub-requirement of REF-BM-02, split from the caught title/desc/favicon correction).

decisions.evidence: R1 spec had only a plain one-line description. R1 client: 'I'd want richer notes on a bookmark — somewhere I can write my own thoughts with a bit of formatting, not just a plain one-line description.' R2 maker: 'Formatted personal notes.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Formatted markdown notes (REF-BM-23) were missing from the presented scope; client requests the related reference requirement — extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec had generic 'search'. R1 client: 'Searching feels too basic. I'd want to search by tag directly ..., combine terms with and/or/not, and search for an exact phrase.' R2 maker: 'Tag qualifiers, exact phrases, Boolean operators, and parentheses in search.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. #tag search (REF-BM-14), AND/OR/NOT + parentheses (REF-BM-15) and exact-phrase (REF-BM-16) were missing from the presented basic search; client requests these reference requirements — extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec had no bulk actions. R1 client: 'I'd want to be able to select a bunch of bookmarks at once and do something to all of them together — tag them, mark them read, or remove them in one go.' R2 maker: 'Multi-selection and bulk actions.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Multi-select bulk actions (REF-BM-20) were missing from presented scope; client requests the reference requirement — extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 spec had no archive. R1 client: 'I'd want to "archive" links to tuck them out of the way without deleting them, and be able to look at the archived pile separately — archiving being something I can undo, unlike delete which is gone for good.' R2 maker: 'Reversible archiving plus explicitly confirmed permanent deletion.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive-to-hide (REF-BM-26), archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27) and separate archive view (REF-BM-28) were missing; client requests these reference requirements — extend.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'imports/exports ... are out of scope.' R1 client: 'being able to pull in bookmarks I already have somewhere else, and get them back out, is something I'll want eventually, so I'd like that noted as coming rather than dropped entirely.' R2 maker: 'Import/export recorded as planned follow-on capabilities.'
decisions.note: Spec gate. Import/export (REF-BM-30/31) were explicitly dropped; client pushes back on 'dropped entirely' and requests the reference requirements be brought into scope as planned — extend (spec-inclusion disposition; distinct in timing/stage from the R5 acceptance below).

decisions.evidence: R5 maker: 'Import/export remains documented for a future release.' R5 client: 'I'm also glad import and export are on the books for later as we agreed — I don't need them today.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. The delivered app diverges from REF-BM-30/31 (import/export not implemented); client explicitly identifies and accepts the departure without requesting alignment — accepted divergence at implementation stage, same reference items as the R1 corrective but a distinct disposition/timing.
